escalation_note: No value was disputed on the full-page read and both sides closed on the first pass; the only crops taken were the mandatory geometry proofs (§3), two of which also served to prove an extrapolated band.

2.measure_note: Landscape sheet rendered portrait: ROW bands are rowbands.py's v_rules_pct, the AMOUNT column band comes from h_rules_pct, and rows advance from HIGH x to LOW x (row 1 is the highest band). rowbands found only 8 vertical rules on this sheet (the printed grid is faint below the data), so the head of the table was identified first — HEADER band [86.20,89.25] and the shaded/hatched spacer band [83.06,86.20], both TRIMMED as non-data (addendum 2026-08-18 §2.2) — and then the pitch, a constant 3.11-3.14 across the four detected data bands, was used to EXTRAPOLATE the fifth and last band as [67.39,70.52]. That extrapolation was then PROVED rather than assumed. cell = the AMOUNT column, the last column of Form A, bounded by the printed rule h=84.81 and the table's bottom border h=95.51. deskew_deg 0.2. PROOF (900 dpi --value): first row pct:79.95,84.81,3.11,10.70@p2 rendered '100' (recorded 100); last row pct:67.39,84.81,3.13,10.70@p2 -- the EXTRAPOLATED band -- rendered '300' (recorded 300), so the extrapolation lands on the right row and not on its neighbour. 'cells' is deliberately OMITTED: only the amount column's two bounding rules were crop-verified, and the interior column boundaries were estimated rather than measured.

3.measure_note: Same rotated-landscape geometry as p2 (axis x, rows high-x to low-x). Header band [84.41,89.37] and hatched spacer band [81.30,84.41] trimmed before index-aligning. Twelve of the thirteen data bands are directly detected at a constant pitch of ~3.06; the thirteenth and last was EXTRAPOLATED as [41.45,44.51] and then proved. cell = the AMOUNT column (last column of Form B), bounded by printed rule h=86.04 and the table's bottom border h=96.74. deskew_deg 0.2. PROOF (900 dpi --value): first row pct:78.21,86.04,3.09,10.70@p3 rendered '28.5' (recorded 28.5); last row pct:41.45,86.04,3.06,10.70@p3 -- the EXTRAPOLATED band -- rendered '69.45' (recorded 69.45). 'cells' omitted for the same reason as p2.

notes: INDEPENDENT RE-READ (2026-08-18 close-out leg). The 2026-08-14 record for this key was withdrawn for geometry defects; that quarantined record was NOT opened and no value was carried from it. Every figure was read fresh off the 200 dpi full-page renders and every band was re-measured and crop-proved. FORM ORDER is the conventional one: p2 = Form A, p3 = Form B. Typed form; candidate and committee secretary are the same person (Leann Kilts) and both signed Oct 27, 2014; RECEIVED stamp OCT 27 2014. THIS IS A PERIOD-SCOPED FILING: the cover's Totals From Last Report column is populated on every line (11,529.11 / 297.45 / 11,826.56 / 0.00), so both schedules itemize only the reporting period and both sides are period-exact, not exact. AMOUNT TYPOGRAPHY: this filer writes ragged decimals -- Form A amounts carry no decimal places at all ('100', '1000') and Form B mixes one-place and two-place figures ('28.5', '99.8', '43.2', '25'). All are transcribed VERBATIM as printed and none was normalised to two places; they sum to the printed totals exactly as written. PRIVACY: Form A prints a full street address in a single Address cell for every donor; only the city/state component is carried, per PRIVACY.md. The address cell is free text and the filer was inconsistent -- two donors have a city with no state and three have 'Ogden Ut' -- so two rows carry a BLANK donor_state that reflects the FILER's omission, not a county redaction. Form B has a City column but no state column, so vendor_state is blank BY THE FORM on all 13 rows. Row 6 of Form B is a payment TO the city of Plain City for park use, so vendor and city are legitimately the same string. Cover line 2's This-Report cell is a bare dash -- a NIL MARK, left BLANK per the zero-glyph ruling, never 0 -- while the line-4 Last-Report cell is a typed '0.00' and is a real zero; the two are different facts on the same cover.
